name: quick-xml
workload: DOM parse, SAX/stream parse, XPath query, and serialize operations on synthetic wide/shallow and deep/narrow XML files sized 1KB-100MB (plus ~10MB DBLP/OpenStreetMap real-world extracts) in the bemayer/xml-benchmark cross-language shootout (14 libraries, 7 languages), each library built and run in its own Docker container on a GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest runner.
claimed_speedup: DOM parse throughput at 10MB: quick-xml 3721.3 MB/s vs pugixml 1575.1 MB/s (2.4x) and libxml2 278.8 MB/s (13.3x); at 100MB: quick-xml 1619.1 MB/s vs pugixml 923.8 MB/s (1.75x) and libxml2 161.2 MB/s (10.0x). SAX/Stream throughput at 100MB: quick-xml 1467.9 MB/s vs libxml2 822.0 MB/s (1.79x). Serialize throughput at 100MB: quick-xml 1581.9 MB/s vs pugixml 1054.0 MB/s (1.5x) and libxml2 551.1 MB/s (2.87x). pugixml instead wins the XPath Query category, which quick-xml does not implement in this suite. (derived from page data)
compiler_and_flags: quick-xml: `cargo build --release` (rustc, default release profile, opt-level=3) inside a rust:slim Docker image; libxml2 and pugixml: g++ via `cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release` inside debian:bookworm-slim Docker images (per benchmarks/<lib>/Dockerfile in the repo)
hardware: GitHub Actions 'ubuntu-latest' hosted runner (exact CPU model not stated; results refresh monthly via a cron CI job)
stars_or_usage: 1.57k stars; one of the most widely depended-on XML crates in the Rust ecosystem
tradeoffs: Written in Rust, so using it from C++ requires FFI/cxx bindings rather than direct linking; primarily an event-based (SAX-like) reader rather than a DOM-first API, though the same benchmark still measured a DOM-parse mode; does not implement XPath querying (pugixml wins that category in the same suite); much of libxml2's loss is tied to its heavier per-node allocation model (peak RSS 933.7 MB vs quick-xml's 106.1 MB at 100MB), so part of the win reflects allocation strategy, not only raw scanning speed.
caveats: Benchmark hardware is a shared GitHub Actions runner with no stated CPU model, which caps the tier at B even though the benchmark code, Docker build steps, and compiler/build-mode flags are all public and reproducible; numbers are regenerated monthly and can drift between runs; the figures above are from the 2026-09-01 run embedded in the published report.
found_via: WebSearch query 'pugixml vs libxml2 benchmark speed comparison XML parser' surfaced github.com/bemayer/xml-benchmark; cross-checked that quick-xml is absent from both the vcpkg ports tree (repos/microsoft/vcpkg/git/trees, 2867 ports) and the conan-center-index recipes tree (1952 recipes) searched for yaml/toml/xml/ini keywords, confirming it as a non-C++ contender found via the benchmark route rather than the C++ package-registry seed query.
